To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount and type of context information have a strong influence on the performance of dialogue act classifiers.

(1) dialogue act recognition performance is highly dependent on the corpus; (2) the influence of context is highly dependent on both the corpus and the type of provided context representation; (3) the influence of the context representation type is highly dependent on corpus; (4) the influence of dialogue act classification context representation is highly dependent on its relative distance to the target dialogue act; (5) the influence of n-grams and n-grams with relative position is highly dependent on dialogue act;

context features are important for the dialogue act recognition problem, and that the best results are obtained when using n-grams of previous utterances and dialogue act classifications, with the latter being more effective than n-grams tagged by relative position.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount and type of context information provided to a classifier has a great influence on the performance of dialogue act recognition.
context information has a significant impact on dialogue act recognition performance and that it is important to explore different representations of it.
